instructions: CLINX forwards messages to native Codex conversations without a reply format contract. Return execution_result.response_text as the original Markdown; do not rewrite it into summary fields. Native COMPLETED records turn completion only; business_outcome=NOT_EVALUATED is not a business PASS. There is one execution backend: native Codex, using its own runtime configuration. When the user supplies codex://threads/... preserve the complete URI including hostId and pass it directly as codex_uri to clinx_prepare_execution. Do not search first, read status first, or call adopt separately. Reuse a known task_ref when no URI is supplied. Only search if the destination is genuinely unknown. The user's request to send or continue work supplies approval; use approved=true without asking for the same approval again. Prepare once, then call clinx_start_execution with the returned prepared_execution_ref and approved=true. Execution stays native Codex. On the Rust connector, an exact thread uses its live native cwd; workspace_contract can otherwise supply an absolute cwd in the target repository. Branch and HEAD snapshots do not gate native forwarding. Independent tasks may share a cwd. Do not put routing requirements only in prompt. Native tasks use full access with no CLINX network gate or filesystem sandbox; legacy network_access flags do not restrict execution. Do not routinely call clinx_get_prepared_request between prepare and start. After a lost response, inspect the ORIGINAL prepared request or exact execution before retrying; never submit another preparation blindly. QUEUED is not Provider running: report execution_started and the returned state accurately. Query status only for progress, results or a concrete conflict. CLINX coordinates task identity and active execution ownership, not operation permissions. Linear is optional audit history. Cancellation uses a managed execution_ref, or a canonical native task_ref with its observed native_turn_id and approved=true. Native cancellation requires the owning node execution scope and remains pending until the native terminal event. For read requests use exact thread_id/codex_uri selectors; do not search the ID as query.

tools.name: clinx_get_effective_authority
tools.description: Read effective FUTURE execution authority for the exact canonical task. Separate policy, operation/target grants, client exposure and runtime health. Discovery never grants authority.

tools.name: clinx_get_prepared_request
tools.description: Read one exact prepared execution or policy change, including immutable content hash, target, scope differences, validity, applied version and exact execution/thread/turn readback. Does not apply, consume or start. Use after lost responses or to resolve a concrete target ambiguity; not a routine prerequisite to start; raw prompts and credentials are not returned.

tools.name: clinx_prepare_policy_reauthorization
tools.description: Prepare a reviewed authority change on the SAME task. New Git target scope must identify a registered task-owned worktree. No execution starts; historical execution policies remain unchanged. Only the outer operator may call this, never the managed worker.

tools.name: clinx_apply_policy_reauthorization
tools.description: Apply exactly one prepared authority change with explicit operator approval, CAS and immutable audit. Idempotent. Active ownership or unresolved side effects block application. Does not execute or replay deployment.

tools.name: clinx_register_derived_git_target
tools.description: Explicit operator registration of one real linked Git worktree for one active task. Supply its successful task Host worktree-add receipt when available; otherwise record explicit operator adoption evidence. Returns a stable target identity; registration alone grants no push.

tools.name: clinx_revoke_derived_git_target
tools.description: Revoke one task-owned Git target. Existing policy history remains immutable; future push fails closed.

tools.name: clinx_adopt_conversation
tools.description: Adopt an exact idle thread visible on the confined Provider. Supply exact_turn_id for a terminal predecessor checkpoint required by Host successor. Does not transfer a Desktop writer.
